decisions.outcome: 3-point MACE (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal stroke), time to first event, ITT, on-study
decisions.span: ITT analyses (on-study and on-treatment) of MACE, defined as cardiovascular death, non-fatal MI, and non-fatal stroke, are consistent with those of MACE+ (Table 8). The reason for the similarity is that only 0.3% of subjects in the ITT population experienced hospitalization for unstable angina. For ITT analysis 792 MACE events were observed, 392 and 400 in placebo and lixisenatide group, respectively. The 95% confidence interval for the hazard ratio is (0.887, 1.172) with a point estimate of 1.02.
decisions.table_span: Table 8: Analysis of the MACE Endpoint | Placebo (N=3,034) | Lixisenatide (N=3,034) | Hazard ratio (95% CI) | MACE endpoint (on-study) 1.02 (0.89, 1.18) | No. of patients with event (%) 392 (12.9%) 400 (13.2%) | Total Person Year 6340.2 6368.7 | Incidence Rate 6.18 6.28
decisions.note: The 4-point primary (1.02 [0.89, 1.17]) and the 3-point secondary (1.02 [0.887, 1.172]) are numerically near-identical because only 0.3% had unstable-angina hospitalisation; older reviews that relabelled the 4-point as 3-point reached the right number by luck. This value is the trial's own 3-point analysis, verified by the FDA statistical reviewer.

decisions.span: The results of the analysis of the composite MACE (a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction and non-fatal stroke) endpoint were consistent with the findings for the primary composite endpoint, with comparable event rates between treatment groups. The HR was 1.02 with an associated upper bound of the 2-sided 95% CI below 1.3.
decisions.rob2_material: SAP-derived: Cox PH prespecified; on-study and on-treatment sensitivity analyses verified by the statistical reviewer; proportional-hazards check (Figure 15); interim analyses at earlier cut-offs reported (pdf p391, p406: MACE point estimate 1.17 at interim) -- available for D2/D5 signalling questions.

decisions.outcome: 3-point MACE (CV death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke), time to first event, ITT, end of study, FREEDOM (CLP-107) only

effect.estimator: Cox proportional hazards regression (CDER review staff; R v4.2; treatment, study and CV risk as strata)

decisions.span: Table 19. Time to First Occurrence of 3-Point MACE (CV Death, Nonfatal MI, Nonfatal Stroke) and 4-Point MACE (CV Death, Nonfatal MI, Nonfatal Stroke, Unstable Angina) - ITT Population End of Study, FREEDOM (CLP-107) | MACE Type | ITCA 650 Number of Events/Total No. (%) IR (n/100 PY) | Control Number of Events/Total No. (%) IR (n/100 PY) | HR (95% CI)** | 3-Point MACE* 85/2075 (4.1%) 2.94 | 69/2081 (3.3%) 2.37 | 1.24 (0.90, 1.70) | 4-Point MACE 95/2075 (4.6%) 3.29 | 79/2081 (3.8%) 2.72 | 1.21 (0.90, 1.63) | Source: CDER Review staff. * One hundred fifty-four positively adjudicated 3-point MACE events. ** Based on a Cox proportional hazards regression model.
decisions.cross_check: 4-point row 95/2075 vs 79/2081, HR 1.21 (0.90, 1.63) equals the Nat Med 2021 abstract (PMID 34873344) primary result -- document identity corroborated at level 1.
decisions.adjudication_of_circulating_values: 1.24 (0.90-1.70) = this FDA end-of-study FREEDOM-only analysis (adopted; level 2); 1.20 (0.88-1.64) = a full-text meta's figure, level 5 pointer, not adopted; 1.21 (0.90-1.63) = the 4-point primary relabelled by some reviews as 3-point -- wrong endpoint. The FDA document also gives end-of-treatment and pooled (CLP-103/105/107) variants; the review's timepoint rule (end of randomised follow-up, trial-only) selects the end-of-study FREEDOM-only row.
decisions.note: CDER concluded FREEDOM is an outlier versus the seven other GLP1RA CVOTs on 3-point MACE (Figure 14/15); ITCA 650 is not approved. This is the trial that decides whether the near-zero heterogeneity on the served page is real.
